text:
sam: Heads-up — after the private VPC rollout at 03:15 we saw a sustained p99 latency jump (~2.5x) and throughput drop on a subset of dedicated nodes. Not a full outage but very noticeable to customers.

maria: Which nodes/region? any hostnames? quick metrics?

sam: vpc-prod-us-west-2, pool-gamma. host examples: gamma-12, gamma-14. p50 stable, p95 up ~1.6x, p99 up ~2.5x. errors are ~0.2% (timeou ts), not request-level failures.

alex: I pulled a flamegraph from one affected host — looks like kernel-selection path and batching decision code are hot. Top of stack is our runtime's kernel_router::choose_fast_path then batch_manager::emit_batch. Link: https://perf.redwood/internal/flame/2158881111 (private)

jean: infra metrics show NAT port exhaustion spikes aligned with the latency window, and ephemeral port reuse increased. Not full conntrack OOM but queueing at the egress proxy.

dev-ex: We shipped a heuristic change to batch_manager in the rollout: changed the size_threshold from 6->4 for low-latency targets and flipped a kernel preference flag that favors the 'vectorized' kernel for short sequences. Could be related.

ops-bot: deploy-bot recorded rollout at 03:12 by @dev-rel; canary to 20% then ramp to 100% in 3m. Rollback available: rollback id c9a2.

maria: Can we get a few quick traces (cpu + network) and a small reproduction test? If batching now emits smaller batches but switches kernel, we might be increasing packet-per-request count, which amplifies NAT usage.

alex: I ran perf top for 60s, pasted the top lines:
```
 12.4% kernel_router::choose_fast_path
 9.8% batch_manager::emit_batch
 8.1% runtime::kv_cache::lookup (lot of misses)
 6.7% iptables->netfilter
 5.3% socket_sendmsg
```

sam: kv cache miss rate spiked concurrently — cache hit rate dropped from 87% -> 62% for this workload. Could be eviction behavior after the batching change (batches shape requests differently).

jean: NAT metrics: ephemeral port utilization for pool-gamma jumped from 42% -> 88% for a brief window. Translation table entries didn't clear fast enough because connections were short-lived but very bursty.

infra-oncall: Could be 'many tiny sockets' pattern now. If batching decreased, we open more sockets per second -> more NAT ports consumed. Also kernel routing to vectorized kernel may be less cache-friendly (more syscalls).

dev-ex: Rolling back the batch size heuristic to 6 in canary might prove it. Also we can force kernel_selector to prefer bulk kernel for affected class to compare.

maria: Proposed short runbook: 1) throttle rollout (pause) 2) rollback batch heuristic in canary -> observe 3) temporary kernel preference override to legacy path on pool-gamma 4) collect flamegraphs + netstat snapshots + ipvs/iptables counters.

sam: I've paused the ramp (ops-bot: pause rollout). Also enabled a per-pool kernel override to legacy on gamma. Noted what changed in deploy logs.

deploy-bot: rollout paused by @sam at 03:21. Override kernel-selector for pool-gamma applied (flag kernel_selector.force=legacy).

alex: After kernel override we see p99 trending down slowly toward baseline (sample window 2m). KV cache miss rate still high though.

jean: I pushed a quick NAT port reclaim tweak to egress-proxy (reduce TIME_WAIT reuse window) for canary hosts; watch for side effects.

dev-ex: We should instrument batch_manager to emit per-batch socket count and per-request socket lifecycle counts (short-term), and add a guard in kernel selection: if ephemeral port utilization > 75% prefer kernel that reduces syscall-per-token.

maria: Agreed. Who owns the follow-ups?

sam: I'll file a perf incident ticket with action items, assign kernel selector + batching to @alex and @dev-ex, NAT tuning to @jean, and infra-oncall to monitor.

alex: I'll create a small benchmark that mimics pico-requests (seq len ~16, concurrency pattern 120/s) to reproduce locally.

jean: I'll run a NAT port stress test against a canary host and validate the reclaim change.

infra-oncall: Monitoring playbook: alert on ephemeral_port_util > 80% for 1m, p99 > baseline * 1.5, kv_cache_hit_rate < 70%. Put runbook links in the ticket.

dev-ex: Quick note: if we revert batching size we may increase token-level cost; coordinate with pricing impact folks.

maria: Sounds good — status check in 45m. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

sam: TL;DR: rollout introduced two correlated changes (smaller batches + kernel preference flip) that increased tiny-socket patterns, amplifying NAT ephemeral port usage and causing p99 latency spikes. Mitigation = pause, kernel override, NAT reclaim tweak, rollback heuristic if needed.

alex: saving logs/profiles to incident folder: s3://incidents/2158881111/

jean: marking follow-ups in ops tracker -> INC-2158881111

infra-oncall: I'll keep an eye and will post updates if anything regresses.

maria: closing for now unless metrics worsen.
